sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 34.8% a year from $404.5 million in FY2016 to $5,931.4 million in FY2025 [F1][F10][F196].
The shape is a decelerating growth curve: 64.2% in FY2021, 11.8% in FY2022, 0.1% in FY2023, then 16.4% and 10.6% in FY2024 and FY2025 [D218][D263][D311][D358][D406].
FY2017's operating loss of $3,485.6 million reflected a $2.6 billion increase in stock-based compensation tied to the CEO award and IPO-related RSUs [F12][P74].
The operating margin bottomed at -422.5% in FY2017 and has since climbed to -9.0% in FY2025, a 413.5pp recovery [F22][F30].
FY2025 revenue rose $570.0 million, split between a $282.4 million advertising increase on ~17% more impressions and a $287.6 million other-revenue increase from subscriber growth [P24].
Advertising contributed 5.3pp of the 10.6% growth and other revenue 5.4pp, lifting other revenue to 12.6% of the total from 4.3% in FY2023 [D538][D545][D406][D543][D539].
North America still supplied 58.6% of revenue in FY2025 but only 4.4pp of growth, while rest of world added 3.7pp [D456][D458][D499].
Operating costs grew 5.1% against 10.6% revenue growth, so revenue grew 5.5pp faster than operating costs [D423][D406][D430].
The incremental operating margin was 44.8% in FY2025, and the diluted share count rose 2.1% while the net loss shrank 34.0% [D429][D425][D408].
The FY2025 operating margin of -9.0% is the window high, against a -32.4% median and a -422.5% low in FY2017 [F30][D555][D553].
The FY2025 margin improved 5.7pp, with cost of revenue adding 1.1pp, R&D 1.3pp and other lines 3.3pp [D419][D431][D432][D433].
The R&D gain came despite a $101.9 million increase in R&D expense, offset by $38.8 million of FY2024 restructuring charges that did not repeat [P23].
In FY2025 net margin of -7.8% sat 1.2pp above the -9.0% operating margin, helped by $68.9 million of other income [F50][F30][D591][X130].
Operating cash flow of $656.2 million in FY2025 exceeded the $460.5 million net loss, and free cash flow reached $437.2 million, a 7.4% margin [F80][F40][F100][D393].
Operating cash flow rose from $413.5 million in FY2024 on non-cash stock-based compensation of $1.0 billion and a $45.9 million increase in accounts payable [P13].
Capex was $219.0 million, or 3.7% of revenue and 1.34x D&A [F90][D392][D395].
Cash generation now rests heavily on $1,016.8 million of stock-based compensation, 155.0% of operating cash flow [X90][D396].
Net cash swung to net debt of $596.3 million in FY2025, or -10.1% of revenue, from net cash of $1,439.8 million in FY2021 [D399][D400][D211].
That net-cash position ranks at the 0th percentile against an internet peer median of 45.0% net cash of revenue (n=5) [D578][D579].
The company repurchased $1.4 billion of notes in February 2025, funded by $1.47 billion of net proceeds from new 2033 Notes [P1][P2].
Buybacks of $750.9 million were 171.7% of free cash flow, and the diluted share count still rose 2.1% [D401][D402][D425].
The company has posted a net loss in each of the last 10 years, from $514.6 million in FY2016 to $460.5 million in FY2025 [R1][F31][F40].
The loss is narrowing but a decade without profit leaves the equity story dependent on continued margin repair [R1].
Stock-based compensation was 17.1% of revenue in FY2025 and at least 10% in each of the last 9 years [R2][D390].
At 191.1% of the operating loss, compensation is the main reason cash flow outruns earnings [R2][D404].
Net cash fell for a fourth straight year into net debt of $596.3 million in FY2025 [R3][D399].
Buybacks above free cash flow in FY2023-FY2025 have funded returns with balance-sheet capacity rather than earnings [R4][D307][D354][D402].
Whether the FY2025 operating margin of -9.0% holds or improves will show in the FY2026 10-K [F30].
Whether net debt of $596.3 million narrows or deepens against the FY2025 level will show in the FY2026 10-K [D399].
Whether stock-based compensation stays below the FY2025 level of 17.1% of revenue will show in the FY2026 10-K [D390].
